days.title: Western and Central Peaks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Kollafjörður
stops.detail: The elongated mountain massif is approx. 20 km long and extends in the narrower sense from Kollafjörður to Hátindur, but actually as far as Kjós to Mount Skálafell, touching the areas of three extinct central volcanoes, namely the Stardal volcano near Kjós (with the center roughly under today's Mount Skálafell), the Kollafjörður volcano and the Hvalfjörður volcano.

stops.name: Kistufell
stops.detail: Particularly striking is Mount Kistufell, which protrudes furthest to the south and is roughly level with Mosfellsbær.

stops.name: Þverfellshorn
stops.detail: The two signposted hiking trails lead to Þverfellshorn and to Kerhólakambur (851 m); helicopter flights for tourists are also offered.

stops.name: Hátindur
stops.detail: The easternmost peak is Hátindur (909 m).

stops.name: Gunnlaugsskarð
stops.detail: For a long time it was also considered the highest peak, but it turned out that the elevation north of Gunnlaugsskarð is even higher, namely 914 m.

stops.name: Moskarðshnúkar
stops.detail: The easternmost peaks of the mountain range, the Moskarðshnúkar, glow unusually brightly.
